title: Birth Certificate (Local Copy)
description: Official certified copy of birth certificate registered in Isabela

sections.heading: Step-by-Step Process
sections.lead: Follow these steps to request your birth certificate

items.title: Check Eligibility
body: You can request if you are the owner, parent/guardian, or authorized representative with proper authorization letter.

items.title: Prepare Documents
body: Bring valid government-issued ID. If representative: authorization letter and IDs of both owner and representative.

items.title: Visit Civil Registrar
body: Go to the Local Civil Registrar Office at 2nd Floor, Provincial Capitol. Office hours: Mon-Fri, 8AM-5PM.

items.title: Fill Out Request Form
body: Complete the request form with full name, date of birth, place of birth, parents' names, and purpose.

items.title: Pay the Fee
body: Pay ₱150 per certified copy at the Provincial Treasurer's Office (same building).

items.title: Claim Certificate
body: Return to Civil Registrar with official receipt. Certificate released within 15-30 minutes if record is available.

sections.heading: Requirements
sections.lead: Documents needed for your application

blocks.title: If You Are a Representative
items: Authorization letter signed by the owner
Valid ID of the representative (original + photocopy)

items.title: Can I get a birth certificate registered in another province?
body: No. The Isabela Civil Registrar only has records for births registered in Isabela. For other municipalities, request from that province's Civil Registrar or from PSA.

items.title: What if I don't know the exact date of birth?
body: Provide an approximate year and month. The staff will help search the records, but this may take longer.

items.title: Can I request through email or online?
body: Currently, requests must be made in person. Online services are being planned for the future.

items.title: What's the difference between local copy and PSA copy?
body: Both are certified true copies. PSA copies are nationally-recognized and required for passport/visa applications. Local copies are accepted for most local transactions and school enrollment.

items.title: Is there a fee for death certificate registration?
body: Registration of death certificate is free of charge, pursuant to Section 6 of P.D. No. 651. However, you need to pay for the Burial Permit (₱50.00) or Transfer Permit (₱100.00).

items.title: What is the deadline for registering a death certificate?
body: The death certificate must be registered within 30 calendar days from the date of death. After this period, it will be considered delayed registration and will require additional documents.

items.title: What is the difference between Burial Permit and Transfer Permit?
body: A Burial Permit (₱50.00) is required if the deceased will be buried in any cemetery in Isabela. A Transfer Permit (₱100.00) is required if the remains will be transferred to another province for burial.

items.title: Who can be the informant for death registration?
body: The informant is usually a family member or relative of the deceased who has knowledge of the facts of death. For hospital deaths, the attending physician provides the medical information.

items.title: How long does the registration process take?
body: For death in hospital/clinic: approximately 1 hour and 38 minutes. For death at home: approximately 1 hour and 35 minutes. This includes time for embalmer certification and PHO review.

title: Marriage Certificate (Local Registration)
description: Registration of Certificate of Marriage at the Local Civil Registrar

text: The Certificate of Marriage (COM) of a Civil or Church wedding with Marriage License must be registered within fifteen (15) days after the solemnization of marriage. COM of a Civil or Church Wedding under Art. 34 or PD 1083 must be registered within thirty (30) days after the solemnization of marriage. Registration of marriage certificate is free of charge, pursuant to Section 6 of P.D. No. 651.

sections.heading: Step-by-Step Process
sections.lead: Follow these steps to register your marriage certificate

items.title: Submit Certificate of Marriage
body: Submit the accomplished Certificate of Marriage (COM) for review. The COM must be duly signed by the contracting parties, solemnizing officer, and at least two witnesses.

items.title: Claim Registered Certificate
body: Get your copy of COM duly registered and signed by the Receiving Officer and PCRC or any authorized signatory. Accomplish Client Feedback Form and drop at designated suggestion box.

sections.heading: Requirements
sections.lead: Documents needed for marriage registration

blocks.title: For Timely Registration (Within 15/30 Days)
items: Certificate of Marriage duly signed by the contracting parties
Signatures of at least two (2) witnesses

blocks.title: For Delayed Registration
items: Affidavit for Delayed Registration of Marriage (at the back of the document shall be accomplished)

Affidavit of the solemnizing officer or the person reporting or presenting the marriage certificate for registration stating the facts and circumstances surrounding the marriage and the reason or cause of delay

items.title: Is there a fee for marriage certificate registration?
body: No. Registration of marriage certificate is free of charge, pursuant to Section 6 of P.D. No. 651.

items.title: What is the deadline for registering a marriage certificate?
body: For Civil or Church wedding with Marriage License: within 15 days after solemnization. For weddings under Art. 34 or PD 1083: within 30 days after solemnization.

items.title: What if I missed the registration deadline?
body: You will need to file for delayed registration. This requires additional documents including a PSA negative certification and an affidavit explaining the reason for the delay.

items.title: Who should sign the Certificate of Marriage?
body: The Certificate of Marriage must be signed by both contracting parties (bride and groom), the solemnizing officer (priest, judge, or governor), and at least two witnesses.

items.title: How long does the registration process take?
body: The total response time is approximately 5 minutes for timely registration with complete documents.

Children in conflict with the law (CICL)

items.title: Family Reintegration
body: Programs to reunite and strengthen family relationships.

items.title: Skills Training
body: Vocational and life skills training for self-sufficiency.

items.title: Aftercare Services
body: Follow-up support and monitoring after rehabilitation.

sections.heading: Supplementary Feeding Program
sections.lead: Nutrition support for malnourished children and vulnerable groups

text: The Supplementary Feeding Program aims to improve the nutritional status of malnourished children aged 0-5 years old through provision of nutritious meals and nutrition education.

items.title: Hot Meals
body: Nutritious hot meals provided daily to beneficiaries.

items.title: Growth Monitoring
body: Regular weighing and height measurement to track progress.

items.title: Nutrition Education
body: Parent education on proper nutrition and child care.

sections.heading: Day Care Services
sections.lead: Early childhood care and development program

text: The Day Care Service Program provides early childhood care and development (ECCD) services to children aged 3-4 years old, preparing them for formal schooling while their parents work.

items.title: Early Learning
body: Age-appropriate educational activities and learning materials.

items.title: Socialization
body: Group activities to develop social skills and interaction.

items.title: Health Monitoring
body: Regular health check-ups and growth monitoring.

items.title: Feeding
body: Nutritious snacks and meals during day care hours.

sections.heading: Self-Employment Assistance - Kaunlaran (SEA-K)
sections.lead: Capital assistance for micro-enterprise development

text: The Self-Employment Assistance - Kaunlaran (SEA-K) program provides capital assistance to disadvantaged individuals and families to start or expand small-scale livelihood projects.

sections.heading: Social Pension for Indigent Senior Citizens
sections.lead: Monthly stipend for qualified elderly citizens

text: The Social Pension Program provides monthly stipend to indigent senior citizens aged 60 years old and above to help augment their daily subsistence and medical needs.

items: Filipino citizen, 60 years old and above
No pension from government or private agencies

sections.heading: Sustainable Livelihood Program (SLP)
sections.lead: Community-based capacity building and livelihood assistance

text: The Sustainable Livelihood Program is a community-based capacity building program that provides participants with training, technical and financial assistance to improve their socio-economic status.

items.title: Microenterprise Development (MD)
body: For participants who want to start or expand their own business. Includes seed capital fund and business development training.

items.title: Employment Facilitation (EF)
body: For participants seeking employment. Includes skills training, job matching, and employment assistance.

sections.heading: Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situation (AICS)
sections.lead: Emergency financial assistance for various needs

text: AICS provides emergency assistance to individuals and families in crisis situations including medical, burial, educational, and transportation assistance.

items.title: Medical Assistance
body: Financial aid for hospitalization, medicines, laboratory tests, and medical procedures.

items.title: Burial Assistance
body: Financial support for funeral and burial expenses of indigent families.

items.title: Educational Assistance
body: Support for school fees, supplies, and other educational needs.

items.title: Transportation Assistance
body: Travel assistance for medical referrals and emergency situations.

title: Tricycle Franchising and Records Sections

sections.heading: Process Flow
sections.lead: Step-by-step procedures for tricycle franchise and records request

items.title: Receiving of Documentary Requirements
body: Submit documentary requirements to the BPLS

items.title: Inspection of Tricycle Unit
body: BPLS Inspector inspects the tricycle unit

items.title: Verification of Records & Fees
body: Franchising Staff verifies records and assessment fees

items.title: Receiving Application Form
body: BPLS Inspector receives the franchise application form

items.title: Governor's Approval
body: Provincial Governor approves the application form

items.title: Collection of Fees
body: Provincial Treasurer's Office collects the fees

items.title: Receiving Notarized Documents
body: BPLS receives notarized application and other documentary requirements

items.title: Encoding of Application
body: BPLS encodes the application into the system

items.title: Preparation of Transmittal
body: BPLS prepares the transmittal letter

items.title: Submission to Sangguniang Panlalawigan
body: Submit transmittal letter and franchise applications to the SB

items.title: Receiving & Sorting
body: Franchising Staff receives, inspects, and sorts applications

items.title: Processing & Certification
body: Franchising Staff processes application and issues certification

items.title: Board Members Approval
body: Sangguniang Panlalawigan Members approve the MTOF

items.title: Official Signing
body: Vice Governor and Presiding Officer sign the approved MTOF

items.title: Releasing of MTOF
body: Franchising Staff releases the MTOF to the applicant

items.title: Receiving Letter of Request
body: VMO/SBO Staff receives the letter of request

items.title: Approval/Disapproval
body: Vice Governor or Secretary to the Sanggunian approves/disapproves the request

items.title: Review & Determination
body: Records Officer II reviews and determines document availability

items.title: Retrieval & Reproduction
body: Records Staff retrieves and reproduces the requested documents

items.title: Releasing & Stamping
body: Records Officer III releases and stamps the requested documents

text: Business Permits and Licensing Section handles tricycle franchise applications and documentary requirements.
